minutes.headline: Personnel Committee approved two new Salary Administration Plan job descriptions, a plow-operator hire and a longevity change.
minutes.summary: The Personnel Committee met remotely and approved the October 29 minutes, a new hire form for a retired DPW worker who plows for the town, and job descriptions for a reserve police officer and a network administrator. It also amended the Salary Administration Plan's longevity language to move from a percentage to flat dollar amounts. Minimum wage compliance was set to return at a following meeting.

votes.motion: Approve the new hire form for Michael Roberts as submitted.
Accept the reserve police officer job description with minor grammatical changes, placed on the Salary Administration Plan.
Accept the network administrator job description at grade 13 as submitted.
Update the Salary Administration Plan to change longevity from a percentage to base pay amounts, section 25.

budget_items.topic: Heavy equipment operator pay for snow plowing hire
budget_items.what_was_said: A retired DPW worker who has plowed for the town since 2004 is to start at a higher step of the pay grade, as the position was previously placed.
The reserve officer was proposed for a grade, which comes closer to the police union pay scale at the top step.
The grade was set as an average of his current pay and comparable communities, and the IT director split shifts toward the town.
Longevity pay changes from a percentage to a flat dollar amount to match the clerical union. Those currently receiving more will be red circled.

decisions.decision: Julie will make the physical and mental requirements wording consistent with the most recent job description format.
Minimum wage compliance for town employees will be taken up at the next meeting or the one after.

what_happened.line: The Personnel Committee amended the Salary Administration Plan so longevity pay moves from a percentage to flat base-pay amounts; the motion passed.
The committee accepted a network administrator job description at grade 13 as submitted.
The committee accepted a reserve police officer job description, with minor grammatical changes, and placed it on the Salary Administration Plan.
The committee approved a new hire form for a retired DPW worker who has plowed for the town since 2004.
Minimum wage compliance for town employees was set for the next meeting or the one after.

why_it_matters: Longevity pay is part of what the town pays long-serving employees, and the change to flat amounts matches the clerical union. Minutes say employees now receiving more will be red circled, so the effect shows over time.
New job descriptions and grades for the reserve police officer and network administrator set pay levels that are paid from the town budget, mostly taxes.
watch_next: Minimum wage compliance for town employees, expected at the next Personnel Committee meeting or the one after.
